clue.text: Lady in Granada gives way on motorway letting queen in

indicators.note: letting someone in means admitting them, so the queen is placed within the other letters

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
to cede is to give way or yield

explanation.surface: A traffic scene: a driver merges on a motorway and lets the queen's car in ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts M first, ahead of CEDES, and the queen is let in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercedes is a common Spanish girl's name, so a woman from Granada could bear it; it is also the car marque that sets the puzzle's theme.

clue.text: It'll pluck hair, from ear and lip to nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the preceding words are scrambled madly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grooming gadget that clears hair from everywhere, ears and lips down to the private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins two pieces of fodder; 'nuts' looks like part of the body list but is the scramble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilator is an electric device that grips and pulls out body hairs by the root.

clue.text: Sports equipment always delivered, and sometimes 6A

definitions.text: Sports equipment always delivered, and sometimes 6A

parts.note: surface reading: kit that is always shipped to the customer, sometimes chauffeured as well
setter's reading: in cricket every ball is delivered by a bowler, and a batter sometimes hits it with a drive

explanation.walkthrough: 6A is DRIVEN; in cricket a drive is a full-blooded forward stroke, and bowling a ball is called delivering it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard leather ball used in cricket is bowled at every delivery and is sometimes struck by an attacking forward shot.

clue.text: Duke flipped for one party trick

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the abbreviation it governs is read backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, means for one

explanation.surface: An aristocrat performs a somersault as his signature trick at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning ruse or scheme, an artful way of getting round something; Dodge is also an American car make.

clue.text: County cricket side turns up in bad mood

indicators.note: in places the reversed side inside the word for a mood

parts.note: a sulk is a fit of bad temper

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the cricket side runs backwards

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field, opposite the leg or on side

explanation.surface: A county cricket team arrives at the ground in a foul temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is a county in eastern England; 'County cricket' looks like one phrase, but County is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is one of the English shires, on the east coast; it also names a breed of sheep, which 25A uses.

clue.text: Daughter with cleavage determined to succeed

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
something riven has been split apart, so it has a cleavage through it

explanation.surface: A daughter wearing a low-cut top is out to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleavage suggests a neckline, but here it means a split, as when rock is cleaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A driven person is highly motivated and ambitious, pushing hard to achieve goals.

clue.text: One paints new car door taupe on the outside

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of taupe

explanation.surface: Someone resprays a new car door, finishing its outside in a greyish-brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator is a tradesperson who paints and papers rooms in houses.

clue.text: Strong feeling Hyundai reliably inspires

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: the end of the car name and the start of the adverb run together

explanation.surface: A Korean car brand's dependability stirs up passionate loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger, a powerful emotion; the word is mostly literary.

clue.text: Show yellow Tesla opens with key

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

indicators.note: the letter that opens a word is its first, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Tesla

explanation.surface: A yellow Tesla car is unlocked with its key fob at a motor show.
explanation.walkthrough: Show looks like a noun for a display, but it is the verb, as in showing a guest to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany or guide them, as when ushering a visitor out; the Ford Escort keeps the car theme.

clue.text: Turn round in one mile, baby

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the following words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: A learner driver is told to do a U-turn within a mile, darling.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby can be an adjective meaning very small, like a mini version of something; the Mini is also a classic small car.

clue.text: 24 wanting icy centre of Halifax fenced off

definitions.note: 24 is SUM, so this reads 'sum wanting'

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of Halifax
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frozen town square in a Yorkshire town has been cordoned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 points to the answer to 24 down, SUM; Halifax is a town in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficiency is a shortfall, the amount by which a total falls short of what is required.

clue.text: American from the east that's scary, no?

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means travelling right to left, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: eek is a cry of fright
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person arriving from the east is frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal name for a person from the United States, especially the north.

clue.text: Official repeatedly touching rope

parts.note: touching, given twice: on, as in 'on the subject of', and re, meaning concerning
a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: A referee or official keeps brushing against the boundary rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on record has been formally noted and made public, and so is officially stated.

clue.text: Faulty Citroen BX valves in odd places that can be changed

indicators.note: something faulty is not working properly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the odd places of a phrase are its first, third, fifth and seventh letters, which are the ones kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these words

explanation.surface: A broken-down French saloon, the Citroen BX, has valves failing in odd spots.
explanation.walkthrough: The BX was a Citroen family car of the 1980s; its X sits in an even place and is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Convertible describes anything able to be transformed into another form; the noun is also a car with a folding roof.

clue.text: Couple back in traffic, vehicle pulling ahead?

indicators.note: in puts the turned pair inside the word for trade

parts.note: truck is an old word for trade or dealings, as in 'have no truck with'

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a pair the other way round

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: Two cars reverse in a traffic jam while another vehicle forges ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed pair goes in after the first letter of the word for trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tow truck is a recovery lorry that hauls broken-down cars, pulling them along in front of the towed vehicle.

clue.text: University well laid out with path, mad being 6A there

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the state of having been driven to madness

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: laying things out arranges them afresh, so the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A campus with a well laid out beside a path, where someone is driven mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 6A is DRIVEN: to be driven up the wall is to be made frantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Up the wall is an informal idiom meaning crazy or furious, the place one is driven by exasperation.

clue.text: Cistern smelled awful without opening

indicators.note: without its opening means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: stank is the past tense of stink

explanation.surface: A water tank gave off a dreadful stench until someone opened it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a container for storing water, which is what a water tank is.

clue.text: Reliable good guy, two thirds of the time right?

indicators.note: keeping two thirds of a six-letter word drops its final two letters

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a very good person
always means all of the time
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a decent man is in the right most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is loyal and dependable, someone who can be counted on.

clue.text: Jazz reversing makes sudden jump forward

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word for the jazz is read from its end

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A driver backs up one moment and lurches forward the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly and swiftly in one direction, a quick dash forward.

clue.text: Navy 8? Well, I'll be given security check shortly

definitions.note: 8 is ESCORT, so this reads 'navy escort'

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
to be vetted is to be screened for security

explanation.surface: A naval recruit is surprised to be screened for security.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is ESCORT; 'Well, I'll be' looks like dialogue but is one exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small warship used to protect convoys; the Chevrolet Corvette also fits the car theme.

clue.text: Petals round bun in California

indicators.note: in puts the circle and the bread inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
O is round in shape
a roll is a bread bun

explanation.surface: A bakery in California tops round buns with flower petals.
explanation.definitionFit: The corolla is the botanical term for all the petals of a flower taken together; Toyota's Corolla keeps the theme.

clue.text: Posher bar with tinned potato?

indicators.note: something tinned is sealed inside a can, so the potato goes inside

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin, so the tin itself supplies these letters
aloo is potato in Indian cooking, as in aloo gobi

explanation.surface: A smart pub serves canned potatoes, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinned works twice: the tin is SN, its chemical symbol, and it holds the potato; a saloon bar was a pub's smarter room in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The saloon bar was traditionally the more comfortable and expensive lounge in a British pub; a saloon is also a car body type.

clue.text: Rue Lilt spraying all over a bespoke suit

indicators.note: all over means covering on every side, so the jumbled letters surround the next word
spraying scatters things about, so the two words are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone splashes Lilt, a soft drink, over a tailor-made suit and regrets it.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilt is a British fruit soft drink; rue doubles as regret and the French for street.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailleur is a woman's tailored suit of matching jacket and skirt, made by a tailor.

clue.text: 6 26s keep swapping sides in street

definitions.note: 6 is DRIVEN and 26 is ANIMAL, so this reads 'driven animals'

indicators.note: one side of the street abbreviation is swapped for its other side within the word

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle, used here for the whole
ST is the abbreviation for street; its two sides are its two letters

explanation.surface: Cars keep switching lanes along a street.
explanation.walkthrough: In CASTLE the S side of ST is replaced by its T side.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are livestock that are herded along by drovers, so they are animals that get driven.

clue.text: Best state south of Massachusetts, an island

parts.note: to cap is to better or top something
Rhode Island, abbreviated RI, borders Massachusetts to the south

explanation.surface: Someone names the finest state just south of Massachusetts, an island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples; the Ford Capri carries the car theme.

clue.text: Rubbish head of MOD's defence work replaced by Conservative

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter is swapped out and the next word's letter put in its place

parts.note: MOD's taken as written; its head, the M, is the letter marked for swapping
a wall is a defensive barrier
op, short for opus, is a work
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A government defence ministry has its chief swapped for a Tory, and the result is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence; its head, the M, is replaced by C.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense or drivel.

clue.text: Problem a few people reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: some means a few

explanation.surface: A handful of people have raised a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an arithmetic problem, the kind set in school.

clue.text: Swedish manufacturer returned calls from 5D, say

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the maker's name is read backwards

parts.note: Saab is the Swedish car and aircraft maker

explanation.surface: A Swedish carmaker has returned calls from Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 5D is SUFFOLK, which is also a breed of sheep, so its calls are bleats.
explanation.definitionFit: Baa is the bleat of a sheep, and Suffolks are a sheep breed, so their calls are baas.

clue.text: Obsessive about one's Jaguar or Beetle, perhaps

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for obsessive goes round the next piece

parts.note: anal is slang for obsessively fussy
one's read as 'one is', and I'm means I am

explanation.surface: A car enthusiast is fanatical about their Jaguar or VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaguar and Beetle look like cars, matching the theme, but here they are a big cat and an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaguar is a big cat and a beetle an insect; both are examples of living creatures.

clue.text: Article that's clear about not drinking Ouzo?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the phrase for clear goes round the next piece

parts.note: 'I see' means 'that's clear', I understand
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is clear that a non-drinker should avoid the Greek spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is loose: ouzo is not anisette, but a similar aniseed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, much like the Greek aperitif ouzo.
